content:
- Overestimate prices when sentiment is positive (especially >0.27) and recent prices are rising — model tends to overshoot.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative or neutral (sentiment <0.27) — model is overly cautious, missing upward momentum.
- Lagged price movements are often over-predicted in the short-term forecast — model reacts too slowly to recent sentiment shifts.
- After a sharp price spike, model tends to overcorrect downward — forecast dips too far below true price.
- Mean reversion bias: model often assumes prices will return to historical averages too quickly, ignoring sentiment-driven momentum.
- Forecast horizon 30d: model consistently overestimates early in the forecast window (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is strong — adjust downward by 1–2% for early periods.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.27–0.53), model fails to capture the “sentiment echo” — forecast lags 1–2 days behind true sentiment-driven moves.
